summary.headline: Pritika Auto Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 31.55% YoY to INR153.19 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 13.85% from 15.99%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue for Q2 FY27 grew 31.55% YoY to INR153.19 crore, supported by higher production volumes (15,665 MT, up about 22%) and OEM programme execution. EBITDA rose 13.97% to INR21.21 crore, but margin compressed about 214 bps YoY to 13.85%, which management attributed to raw material (scrap and pig iron) price spikes not yet passed through. Margin improved sequentially from 13.45% in Q1 FY27. PAT rose 12.41% to INR7.43 crore. Management flagged an export order via subsidiary Pritika Engineering Components and a target of 1 lakh MT installed capacity by end-2028.

segments.name: Tractor components (core)
segments.commentary: Primary business; supplies Mahindra & Mahindra, Mahindra Swaraj, TAFE, Escorts Kubota and CNH Industrial. Management said about 93% of business is tractor-linked, with CV at about 7%.

segments.name: Commercial vehicles
segments.commentary: About 7% of business. Already supplying Ashok Leyland, with plans to expand product portfolio and volumes there.

segments.name: Pritika Engineering Components (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: About 23-25% of current capacity per management, expected to rise to 30-35% in 1-1.5 years. Secured INR12 crore per annum Italian export order; KION USA product approved with production expected in FY27-28.

segments.name: Railways (new initiative)
segments.commentary: Developing 2-3 components; RDSO route to start by Jan-Feb 2027, with supplies targeted from Sep-Oct 2027 (H2 FY28).

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth target of 15% to 20% YoY over the coming years.
EBITDA margin target of 14% to 15%, with slight upside once Lost Foam Casting (LFC) is streamlined.
Raw material cost increases are passed through with a one-quarter lag, so management expects better Q3 margins.
Exports to contribute minimum 10% to 15% of sales within 3 to 5 years; Italian order could grow from INR12 crore to INR40-50 crore in 3 years.
Installed capacity to reach 80,000 MT by end-Nov 2026 (7,800 MT addition) and 1 lakh MT by end-2028 (further 24,000 MT, land acquisition in progress).
Q3 is seasonally lower than Q2 due to planned maintenance in December and post-Diwali demand drop, but October 2026 retail was reported as flat with last October.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume growth, export wins and long-term capacity targets, but defensive when pressed on margin compression, expense breakdown and ROE trend, where answers were brief and deflected to seasonality and raw material pass-through.
key_quotes: Our production volume for Q2 FY27 stood at 15,665 metric tons compared to 12,881 metric tons in the corresponding quarter last year, registering a growth of approximately 22%.
We continue to work towards our long-term target of achieving installed capacity of 1 lakh metric tons by year 2028.
And that -- I mean, we -- what we expect in next 3 to 5 years, exports should contribute minimum 10% to 15% of our sales.
Basically, that is the raw material prices. In Q2, there was a lot of increase in raw material prices, which normally are passed on by next month, next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: How does management see export growth over the next 2-3 years and what share of revenue is targeted?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said exports have potential in Europe and the USA; the Italian order of INR12 crore per annum could reach INR40-50 crore in 3 years, and exports should contribute a minimum 10-15% of sales in 3-5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA grow only about 14% when revenue grew about 31% in Q2, and what is the pass-through period?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to a sharp rise in raw material prices (scrap and pig iron) in Q2, which is passed on with a one-quarter lag, so Q3 margins should improve.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected utilisation and return profile of the capacity investments?
qa_highlights.answer: Green sand capacity is running at about 90% and LFC at about 50%; 7,800 MT is being added by end of the month, and the balance-sheet plan is a combination of debt (major part) and equity.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the increase in other expenses (INR28 crore to about INR34 crore) and interest expense (INR5.60 crore to INR6.33 crore)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said other expenses rose in line with sales, and interest rose in line with growth; as a percentage it had reduced from 25% (answer brief, no breakdown given).

qa_highlights.question: What is the expansion roadmap to 1 lakh MT capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity moves to 80,000 MT with 7,800 MT by end of November; another 24,000 MT is planned by 2028 after land acquisition, with 2027 as the construction year and 1 lakh MT by end-2028.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue and margin guidance over the next couple of years?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue growth target of 15-20% YoY; EBITDA margin target of 14-15%, with slight upside once LFC is streamlined.

qa_highlights.question: Why have ROE and net debt-to-equity fluctuated, and is leverage rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said debt-to-equity is 0.67 and not rising sharply; the CFO said basic ROE is in line with last year, and the debt-equity mix changes on average debt as capital and debt are raised for expansion.

capex_capacity: Installed capacity is 72,000 MT per annum across Punjab and Himachal Pradesh facilities; an additional 7,800 MT (about 650 MT per month) is due by end-Nov 2026, taking capacity to 80,000 MT.

A further 24,000 MT is planned by March 2028 (calendar 2028 per management clarification), with land acquisition in progress and next year (2027) as the construction period; target is 1 lakh MT installed capacity by end-2028.
Utilisation: green sand lines at about 90%; LFC (lost foam casting) lines at about 50%.
Pritika Engineering Components expansion expected ready by end of the current month (Nov 2026); a greenfield new location and plant is planned beyond that.
Capex for the railway initiative is said to be almost complete after about 1.5 years of work.
Funding: management said the expansion will be a combination of debt and equity, with major part debt; consolidated net debt-to-equity was 0.67 in FY26 and is expected to rise.

Solar power MoU with Spark Grid Private Limited (Aug 2026) for supply over 25+ years; group savings about INR110 crore, about INR70 crore to PEC and Meeta Castings and balance to PAIL; SPV with PEC holding 26% equity, subject to approvals.
demand_pricing: Q2 FY27 production volume 15,665 MT vs 12,881 MT in Q2 FY26 (+approximately 22%); H1 FY27 production about 30,000 MT vs 25,267 MT (+nearly 19%).

Customer base: Mahindra & Mahindra, Mahindra Swaraj, TAFE, Escorts Kubota, CNH Industrial; repeat and incremental business received from M&M, Swaraj, CNH and Escorts in the quarter. Relationship tenures cited: M&M over 22 years, Escorts over 50 years, TAFE 28 years.
Mix: about 93% tractor-linked and about 7% CV; already supplying Ashok Leyland with plans to expand portfolio and volumes.

Export: Pritika Engineering Components (subsidiary) secured an Italian precision engineering order of about INR12 crore per annum (in discussion about 7-8 months); potential to grow to INR40-50 crore in 3 years. KION USA product approved by customer; regular production expected in FY27-28.

Margin pressure: management attributed EBITDA margin decline to raw material (scrap and pig iron) price increases in Q2; pass-through on a one-quarter lag. Q2 EBITDA margin 13.85% vs 15.99% YoY and 13.45% in Q1 FY27.

Demand outlook: Q3 seasonally lower than Q2 due to December planned maintenance and post-Diwali drop, though last year Q3 was up. October 2026 retail described as equal to last October. Management said the tractor industry is primarily domestic and largely insulated from geopolitics.

Product mix: moving from small and medium castings into large castings (e.g., a 530 kg SG iron casting developed via LFC, previously imported from China), where competition is fewer and value addition higher. Railways: 2-3 components under development, RDSO route by Jan-Feb 2027, supplies targeted Sep-Oct 2027.
risks_watch: EBITDA margin remains below prior-year levels (13.85% vs 15.99%), and management relies on raw material pass-through with a one-quarter lag; watch whether Q3 margin improves as guided.
Q3 seasonality: December planned maintenance and post-Diwali demand drop; management said the numbers would be clearer in about 1-1.5 weeks.
Rising leverage: net debt-to-equity at 0.67 in FY26 with management expecting it to increase as debt funds the 24,000 MT expansion.
Execution on the 7,800 MT addition by end-Nov 2026 and the 24,000 MT plan by 2028, including land acquisition, which is still in progress.
Export and new-business timelines: KION USA production in FY27-28, Italian order ramp, and railway RDSO route (Jan-Feb 2027) with supplies from Sep-Oct 2027.
Expenses and ROE questions were answered briefly without a breakdown; the other expense and interest drivers and ROE trend remain unexplained.

adds.what: 7,800 MT addition taking installed capacity from 72,000 MT to 80,000 MT (Punjab and Himachal Pradesh)
24,000 MT further capacity to reach 1 lakh MT by end-2028 (land acquisition in progress)
Pritika Engineering Components expansion (subsidiary) ready by end Nov 2026
Railway components initiative: RDSO route Jan-Feb 2027, supplies Sep-Oct 2027

growth.why: Medium-term guidance of 15-20% revenue growth is backed by a 7,800 MT addition due end-Nov 2026 (+10.8%) and a 24,000 MT expansion to 1 lakh MT by end-2028 with land acquisition in progress, though the 2028 phase has no capex figure and green sand lines already run at ~90% utilisation; the margin target was cut to 14-15% from 15-16%.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin fell to 13.85% from 15.99% YoY on scrap and pig iron spikes, with management guiding a one-quarter pass-through lag so Q3 should improve, but the 14-15% target sits only at the low end of current levels and Q3 is seasonally weaker.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 7,800 MT addition (about 10.8% of 72,000 MT) is under construction and due by end-Nov 2026, taking installed capacity to 80,000 MT; a further 24,000 MT to 1 lakh MT is targeted by end-2028.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 FY27 production rose about 22% to 15,665 MT and H1 about 19%, with repeat business from M&M, Swaraj, CNH and Escorts, and green sand lines already at about 90% utilisation, so the new 7,800 MT should absorb demand.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Green sand lines run at about 90% utilisation and the 24,000 MT expansion is in land acquisition with 2027 as the construction year, so a formal capex announcement is a natural next step, funded by a major debt component.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Revenue growth target of 15-20% was only held and margin target was cut to 14-15%, and management leaned on pass-through timing rather than raising guidance.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Margin guidance was already cut to 14-15% from 15-16%, and H1 margin of 13.66% sits below the band, so further raw material pressure or a slow Q3 could force another cut.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: KION USA product approved with regular production expected in FY27-28, a 530 kg SG iron large casting is being moved into, and railway components reach RDSO route by Jan-Feb 2027 with supplies from Sep-Oct 2027.

rows.label: Italian export order ramp to INR40-50 crore in 3 years
rows.why: Italian order is secured at about INR12 crore per annum and could grow to INR40-50 crore in 3 years, with exports targeted at a minimum 10-15% of sales in 3-5 years, though no timeline beyond the initial order is firm.

rows.label: Rising leverage from debt-funded expansion
rows.why: Net debt-to-equity was 0.67 in FY26 and management expects it to rise as major debt funds the 24,000 MT expansion, with interest expense already up to INR6.33 crore from INR5.60 crore.

rows.label: Solar power supply via Spark Grid SPV
rows.why: Solar MoU (Aug 2026) with Spark Grid targets group savings of about INR110 crore over 25+ years, about INR70 crore to PEC and Meeta Castings, but the SPV with PEC holding 26% is subject to approvals.

tone.note: Management was confident on volume growth (Q2 production +22%), export wins and the 1 lakh MT capacity target, but turned defensive on the margin fall to 13.85%, the expense and interest breakdown, and ROE trend, where analysts pushed and answers were brief.
